epigraph.quote: Refusing to buy a great company when its trend is broken and its post-reclaim risk-reward fails our 1.5:1 gate is not pessimism—it is the core discipline that keeps capital intact for true asymmetric setups.
epigraph.author: Capital Preservation Maxim

web_blocks.html: An unbiased decision weighs both sides before enforcing our quantitative gates. The Bull Steelman: JPMorgan Chase owns America's top deposit and payments moat [1]. It compounded TBVPS at 8.5% over a decade and earned 20% reported ROTCE (21% adjusted) in Q3 2026 [1, 28, 35]. AWM runs $5.21 trillion in AUM ($7.90 trillion client assets at 45% ROE) [28]. Deposit funding costs 2.13% on interest-bearing balances, backed by $1.51 trillion in liquidity [28]. If Treasury yields ease to heal -$19.82B AOCI losses and $50B buybacks restart alongside a 2027 deal boom, peak 22.5% ROTCE (or 8.9% CoE) supports 3.16x $126.00 forward TBV = $398.00 stated ($374.84 HTM-adjusted; $357.00 at 20.5% ROTCE and 9.5% CoE).

The Bear Steelman: Fortress banks still suffer multiple compression when capital flexibility tightens. Q3 2026 footnotes exposed -$19.82B in AOCI losses and $25.84B in unrecorded HTM bond marks (-$7.38/sh after tax) [28]. Management paused buybacks in August and September while FY2026 expense guidance climbed to ~$108.6B [28, 35]. Ahead sit a 5.5% 2028 G-SIB surcharge, ~6% Basel III CET1 inflation, and ~$24B/$106.7B Apple Card commitments [28, 32]. The firm also holds $449.1B in NBFI/SPE wholesale exposure while Marianne Lake and CFO Jeremy Barnum hand off leadership to Petno, Rohrbaugh, and Bregje de Best [28, 29, 30]. If unemployment climbs and Card NCOs exceed 4.0%, ROTCE compresses toward 15.5% (2.00x at 9.5% CoE)—pulling shares to $233.00 stated ($218.24 HTM-adjusted).

web_blocks.html: We separate business quality from capital deployment across all three investment horizons. On the Short-Term (1–12 weeks) horizon, JPM sits in Stage 4 on 1.73x distribution volume with 4H RSI at 21.97 and no upward turn [34]. Tactical trading capital therefore stays completely sidelined. On the Medium-Term (6–18 months) horizon, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0: TREND, VALUATION). At $310.68, shares trade above both our $302.75 stated and $284.30 HTM-adjusted Base values, while reclaiming $334.16–$337.35 over a $315.27 Pivot S2 stop (2.39x–2.79x ATR) offers negative reward-to-risk (< 0:1). That fails both our Stage 4 ceiling (CAP_REJECTED) and our 1.50:1 anti-hedging gate. On the Long-Term (3–5+ years) horizon, JPM keeps its COMPOUNDER_PASS quality rating on our watchlist until a Stage 1/2 base forms with ≥1.50:1 asymmetry.

What Would Upgrade This REJECTED Verdict: JPM must first complete a multi-week Stage 1 base AND either reclaim its 30-week and 50-day SMAs ($334.16–$337.35) on >1.2x volume with Base fair value lifted above $371 (via AOCI healing and resumed >$5B quarterly buybacks) OR form a lower Stage 2 base whose structural stop yields ≥1.50:1 asymmetry anchored to HTM-adjusted TBVPS ($105.26 current / $113.72 forward). book_paragraphs: After auditing ten years of balance sheets, Q3 2026 footnotes, a Gordon Growth Reverse DCF, and multi-timeframe charts, it is time to make an unhedged capital decision. Let us steelman both sides fairly. On the Bull side, JPMorgan Chase remains America's widest-moat universal bank. It earns 20% reported ROTCE, oversees $5.21 trillion in AWM assets ($7.90 trillion client assets at 45% segment ROE), funds deposits at 2.13% interest-bearing cost, and backs $1.78 trillion of uninsured deposits with $1.51 trillion in liquid assets. If Treasury yields fall to heal -$19.82 billion of AOCI marks while $50 billion buybacks restart, peak 22.5% ROTCE (or 8.9% CoE) supports 3.16x $126.00 forward TBV, or $398.00 stated ($374.84 HTM-adjusted; $357.00 at 20.5% ROTCE and 9.5% CoE).

On the Bear side, real fundamental and technical friction has surfaced since mid-2026. Adjusted annual expense guidance jumped to ~$108.6 billion across nearly 323,000 staff. Management halted share buybacks in August and September 2026 ($664 million net Q3) as risk-weighted assets expanded $195.8 billion YTD. Ahead lie a 5.5% 2028 G-SIB surcharge, ~6% Basel III CET1 inflation, -$7.38 per share in tax-effected HTM bond marks, ~$24 billion of CECL-covered Apple Card commitments ($106.7 billion unfunded lines), $449.1 billion of NBFI/SPE wholesale exposure, and CFO Jeremy Barnum's 2027 handoff to Bregje de Best. If credit card losses top 4%, ROTCE compresses toward 15.5% (2.00x TBV at 9.5% CoE), pulling shares to $233.00 stated ($218.24 HTM-adjusted).

Weighting those reconciled paths—20% Bull ($398.00), 55% Base ($302.75 at 2.50x $121.10 TBV), and 25% Bear ($233.00 at 2.00x $116.50 TBV)—produces a 12-month probability-weighted expected value of $304.36 stated (-2.03% below $310.68). On HTM-adjusted TBV ($374.84 Bull / $284.30 Base / $218.24 Bear), expected value drops to $285.89 (-7.98%). Meanwhile, JPMorgan sits in Stage 4 below its 50-day, 30-week, and 200-day moving averages on 1.73x distribution volume during an S&P 500 Downtrend.

When we apply our anti-hedging gate without bias, the verdict is unambiguous: REJECTED (TIER_0, driven by TREND and VALUATION). Why not hedge with Wait for Support? Because a genuine Stage 2 exit from Stage 4 requires reclaiming $334.16 to $337.35 above a real structural stop at Pivot S2 ($315.27), while our reconciled 2.50x Base fair value ($302.75 stated / $284.30 HTM-adjusted) sits below both today's $310.68 close and that reclaim band—yielding negative asymmetry (< 0:1).

book_subsections.title: Why Holding Zero Shares and 100% Marginal Cash Is the Right Discipline
paragraphs: First, verify our physical portfolio ledger as of November 20, 2026: we hold zero shares of JPMorgan Chase across Charles Schwab and Robinhood (NOT_HELD, zero shares to sell). Note that JPM's drop to $310.68 decisively breached our prior November 13 structural stop of $322.51. If any position had been open, that breach would have forced an exit; because we held zero shares and stayed patient last week, our capital avoided a 10.3% weekly drawdown.

Second, examine how we allocate our next marginal dollar of US cash ($2,540.35 available across $75,110.60 total US net worth). Our portfolio already carries a 234.2% effective beta-weighted exposure to the S&P 500 while the market sits in a Downtrend with 10 distribution days. Shortlist peer AbbVie (ABBV, Stage 2 at $286.20, 1.52:1 snapshot-zone R:R to $340.00 over a $249.53 stop) stays at 0% allocation to preserve cash during the Downtrend, while outside peer Cheniere Energy (LNG, Stage 2 at $294.84) is already REJECTED at its $315.00 Base target (0.57:1 snapshot-zone R:R over $262.23) and likewise receives 0% allocation.

Notice how clean the portfolio math becomes when you respect both cash preservation and beta exposure. Across our $75,110.60 consolidated US net worth, equities and options already generate $175,884.92 of effective S&P 500 exposure (234.2% beta-weighted exposure). Adding a Stage 4 bank into a 10-distribution-day Downtrend would only amplify drawdown risk while shrinking our $2,540.35 cash cushion. Holding 100% of that marginal cash in reserve is an active, protective choice.

book_subsections.title: Exact Conditions That Would Bring JPMorgan Back Off the Bench
paragraphs: Assigning REJECTED to JPMorgan's stock setup does not mean writing off JPMorgan's business. On business quality, JPMorgan retains COMPOUNDER_PASS. It simply means the combination of a Stage 4 breakdown and a reconciled $302.75 stated ($284.30 HTM-adjusted) Base Case leaves negative post-reclaim upside to justify allocating new capital right now.

Watch two concrete checkpoints before re-underwriting JPMorgan for capital deployment: first, a multi-week Stage 1 bottoming base must form AND either reclaim the 30-week and 50-day moving averages ($334.16–$337.35) on heavy volume or build a lower Stage 2 base; and second, the setup must offer at least 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk anchored to HTM-adjusted TBVPS ($105.26 current / $113.72 forward)—either via AOCI healing and resumed $5B+ quarterly buybacks lifting Base value above $371, or via a deeper reset below intrinsic value. Until both price and valuation realign, keep your cash dry and your discipline intact.

In closing, remember why this two-pass refresh worked as designed. Pass 1 stripped away every prior target and stop so we could uncover the Q3 -$19.82B AOCI mark, $25.84B unrecorded HTM loss, August–September buyback halt, ~$108.6B expense guide, $449.1B NBFI/SPE wholesale exposure, and November 17 CFO transition without confirmation bias. Pass 2 then reconciled Gordon Growth math strictly (2.50x Base = $302.75 stated / $284.30 HTM-adjusted; 2.00x Bear = $233.00 / $218.24) alongside JPMorgan's Stage 4 breakdown at $310.68—producing an unhedged REJECTED (TIER_0) verdict that protects your capital.
